authors: Rudnick, D. L.
title: Ocean research enabled by underwater gliders
summary_own_words: A review of what underwater gliders had achieved in ocean science up to 2016, from submesoscale and biogeochemical studies to measurements of internal waves and turbulence. Useful background for the motivation slide: what gliders are and what science they make possible.
supports_project_part: Slide 1-2 motivation; justification of the slow-vehicle (V~0.3 m/s) setting
limitation: Oceanographic-science focus; says little about navigation or path-planning algorithms.
verification_note: Search returned the Annual Reviews record plus marineinfo.org and peeref records; title, author, volume, pages and DOI agree.

authors: Zeng, Z.; Lian, L.; Sammut, K.; He, F.; Tang, Y.; Lammas, A.
title: A survey on path planning for persistent autonomy of autonomous underwater vehicles
summary_own_words: Surveys how AUV paths are represented and optimised, how paths are re-planned when the environment changes, and how several AUVs plan together, with path planning framed as the key to long (persistent) missions. Gives the vocabulary for the classical side of the project.
supports_project_part: Related-work slide; positioning of the A*/Dijkstra baseline
limitation: Written in 2015, before deep RL became common in this area.
verification_note: Flinders University research portal + library records; author list, volume/pages and DOI agree.

authors: Panda, M.; Das, B.; Subudhi, B.; Pati, B. B.
title: A comprehensive review of path planning algorithms for autonomous underwater vehicles
venue: International Journal of Automation and Computing 17(3):321-352
summary_own_words: Reviews single- and multi-AUV path-planning methods, grouped by whether the underwater environment is treated as predictable or unpredictable. It points out that many classical planners assume the environment is known in advance, which is a poor fit for changing ocean conditions.
supports_project_part: Deep-read survey; taxonomy for the related-work slide; why a learned policy is worth testing
limitation: Published 2020, so it misses the 2021+ deep-RL-in-flow papers listed below.
verification_note: Springer article page returned by search; four authors, issue, pages and DOI confirmed (also OUCI record).

authors: Hong, L.; Liu, L.; Peng, Z.; Zhang, F.
title: Control of marine robots in the era of data-driven intelligence
venue: arXiv:2506.21063 (review; the manuscript template targets Annu. Rev. Control Robot. Auton. Syst. - final DOI not confirmed)
summary_own_words: A recent review of control for single and cooperative marine robots that sorts data-driven methods into model-based, model-free (including RL) and hybrid approaches, and lists open-source resources. Its conclusion is that learning complements rather than replaces classical control, with data efficiency, interpretability and on-board deployment still open.
supports_project_part: Recent-survey slide; framing RL as complement to planners
limitation: Focuses on low-level control more than flow-exploiting route planning; cite the arXiv version unless the journal DOI is found.
verification_note: arXiv abstract page returned by search (submitted 26 Jun 2025, cs.RO); authors confirmed.

authors: Cai, W.; Wang, G.; Zhang, Y.; Qu, X.; Huang, Z.
title: Reinforcement learning for active matter
summary_own_words: Reviews how RL has been used to find motion strategies for single self-propelled particles and to control swarms, which is where most 'navigate through a flow with RL' papers come from. Lists open problems such as generalising across systems.
supports_project_part: Survey of the RL-in-flows lineage (Reddy, Biferale, Gunnarson)
limitation: Microswimmer/active-matter focus; no vehicle energy model or ocean-scale setting.
verification_note: arXiv abstract page; journal reference 'Biophysics Rev. 2025, 6, 031302' as listed on arXiv (journal DOI not opened).

authors: Zermelo, E.
title: Über das Navigationsproblem bei ruhender oder veränderlicher Windverteilung
venue: ZAMM - Zeitschrift für Angewandte Mathematik und Mechanik 11(2):114-124
summary_own_words: The original statement of the navigation problem: a craft with fixed speed relative to the air (or water) must choose its heading over time to reach a target as fast as possible in a known wind (or current) field. Every 'Zermelo' paper in this list starts here.
supports_project_part: Problem-statement slide; the name of the project
limitation: In German; deterministic, fully known flow, minimum time only (no energy).
verification_note: Wikipedia citation, MaRDI portal and C. Fraser's history paper agree on volume, issue, pages and DOI.

authors: Leonard, N. E.; Graver, J. G.
title: Model-based feedback control of autonomous underwater gliders
summary_own_words: Derives a nonlinear dynamic model of a buoyancy-driven glider and uses it to analyse steady glide paths and design feedback controllers in the vertical plane, illustrated on a lab-scale glider. It is the standard reference for 'how a glider actually flies'.
supports_project_part: Glider-model slide; justification (and limitation) of the 2-D kinematic, constant-speed abstraction
limitation: Vertical-plane dynamics only; says nothing about horizontal routing in currents.
verification_note: Princeton author PDF and Princeton research-portal record; DOI from IEEE record.

authors: Garau, B.; Alvarez, A.; Oliver, G.
title: Path planning of autonomous underwater vehicles in current fields with complex spatial variability: an A* approach
summary_own_words: Applies A* graph search on a grid to plan AUV routes through spatially varying (static) current fields, with edge costs based on travel time. This is essentially the classical baseline the project builds.
supports_project_part: Planner-baseline slide (A*/Dijkstra with current-aware edge costs)
limitation: Static 2-D currents, time cost only, result depends on grid resolution.
verification_note: Crossref record (via search) and bibsonomy entry; DOI and pages agree. Full text not opened.

authors: Shadden, S. C.; Lekien, F.; Marsden, J. E.
title: Definition and properties of Lagrangian coherent structures from finite-time Lyapunov exponents in two-dimensional aperiodic flows
summary_own_words: Defines Lagrangian coherent structures as ridges of the finite-time Lyapunov exponent field, i.e. the hidden 'walls' that organise how fluid moves. Its first worked example is the analytic double-gyre stream function that the project uses as its held-out test field.
supports_project_part: Double-gyre held-out test field; stream-function slide
limitation: Kinematic toy flow, not ocean dynamics; theory-heavy for a first read.
verification_note: Caltech AUTHORS record + MaRDI; Shadden lab LCS tutorial confirms the double gyre is the first example.

authors: Lolla, T.; Lermusiaux, P. F. J.; Ueckermann, M. P.; Haley, P. J., Jr.
title: Time-optimal path planning in dynamic flows using level set equations: theory and schemes
summary_own_words: Shows that the set of points a vehicle can reach grows like a front that obeys a modified level-set equation, so the time-optimal path can be traced back from where the front first touches the goal. Validated on a Rankine vortex and applied to unsteady double-gyre and island-wake flows.
supports_project_part: 'Optimal reference' slide; explains what an exact Zermelo solver looks like vs RL
limitation: Needs the full current field (forecast) in advance; minimises time, not energy.
verification_note: MIT DSpace record (author manuscript) + MSEAS group page; volume/pages/DOI agree.

authors: Kularatne, D.; Bhattacharya, S.; Hsieh, M. A.
title: Going with the flow: a graph based approach to optimal path planning in general flows
summary_own_words: Builds a graph over the domain and runs graph search to get both time-optimal and energy-optimal paths in static and time-varying flows, tested on analytic flows, real ocean data and a lab flow tank. The closest classical analogue to the project's 'time-optimal vs energy-aware planner'.
supports_project_part: Energy-aware planner baseline; edge-cost design
limitation: Requires the flow to be known; accuracy limited by graph discretisation.
verification_note: Author PDF on UPenn SCALAR lab site + Lehigh project page; RSS 2016 conference version also exists.

authors: Ng, A. Y.; Harada, D.; Russell, S.
title: Policy invariance under reward transformations: theory and application to reward shaping
summary_own_words: Proves that adding a shaping reward of the form gamma*Phi(s') - Phi(s) never changes which policy is optimal, and that this potential-based form is essentially the only safe additive shaping. This is the theory behind the project's progress-shaping term.
supports_project_part: Reward-design slide; why shaping by distance-to-goal does not change the optimum
limitation: Says nothing about how to choose a good potential; the guarantee assumes the discounted form is used exactly.
verification_note: ML Anthology record + UT Austin reading-list page; pages confirmed (no DOI exists).

authors: Reddy, G.; Celani, A.; Sejnowski, T. J.; Vergassola, M.
title: Learning to soar in turbulent environments
summary_own_words: Trains a simulated (air) glider with the SARSA reinforcement-learning algorithm to climb in turbulent thermals, under realistic flight constraints. The learned policy becomes more cautious as turbulence grows, and the study identifies which sensory cues are worth using.
supports_project_part: Early evidence that RL can learn to exploit a flow; 'RL in flows' history slide
limitation: Atmospheric thermal soaring with tabular RL; aerial glider, not underwater, and no point-to-point goal.
verification_note: PNAS DOI page + PMC4995969 + Princeton portal; authors, volume, pages agree. Topic verified as requested.

authors: Schulman, J.; Wolski, F.; Dhariwal, P.; Radford, A.; Klimov, O.
title: Proximal policy optimization algorithms
summary_own_words: Introduces PPO, a policy-gradient method that alternates between collecting experience and taking several minibatch gradient steps on a 'clipped' objective that stops each update from moving the policy too far. It keeps most of TRPO's stability while being much simpler to implement.
supports_project_part: Method slide (PPO); hyperparameter defaults
limitation: Benchmarked on Atari/MuJoCo; performance is sensitive to implementation details not in the paper.
verification_note: arXiv abstract page; five authors confirmed.

authors: Biferale, L.; Bonaccorso, F.; Buzzicotti, M.; Clark Di Leoni, P.; Gustavsson, K.
title: Zermelo's problem: optimal point-to-point navigation in 2D turbulent flows using reinforcement learning
summary_own_words: Uses an actor-critic RL algorithm to steer a fixed-speed vessel between two points in a 2-D turbulent flow, both frozen and time-evolving. RL finds near-optimal routes, and the classical optimal-navigation solution turns out to be too unstable to use in practice, while RL policies are more robust to noise and to slow vessels.
supports_project_part: Closest classic precedent: Zermelo + RL; 'why not just solve the optimal control' slide
limitation: Minimises time only (no energy); single flow type; small vessel-to-flow geometry.
verification_note: arXiv abstract (v1, v2) lists Chaos DOI; topic verified as requested. Article number 103138 from the DOI record as cited - open the DOI to confirm.

authors: Gunnarson, P.; Mandralis, I.; Novati, G.; Koumoutsakos, P.; Dabiri, J. O.
title: Learning efficient navigation in vortical flow fields
summary_own_words: Trains a fixed-speed swimmer with deep RL to go point-to-point through an unsteady cylinder wake. A policy that senses local flow velocity reaches the target almost every time and approaches the travel time of a global optimal-control planner, clearly beating a policy that senses vorticity.
supports_project_part: Deep-read method paper; observation design (local current); RL-vs-planner comparison
limitation: One flow (cylinder wake); time objective only, no energy model; no unseen-flow test.
verification_note: Nature article page + PMC8654940 + arXiv 2102.10536; topic verified as requested. Open access.

authors: Buzzicotti, M.; Biferale, L.; Bonaccorso, F.; Clark di Leoni, P.; Gustavsson, K.
title: Optimal control of point-to-point navigation in turbulent time dependent flows using reinforcement learning
venue: AIxIA 2020 - Advances in Artificial Intelligence, LNCS 12414, pp. 223-234 (Springer, 2021)
summary_own_words: Follow-up to the Chaos paper that contrasts the deterministic optimal-navigation solution with stochastic RL policies in time-dependent turbulence. Actor-critic RL again finds near-optimal paths in both frozen and chaotic flows.
supports_project_part: Supports claim that RL is competitive with optimal control in time-varying flow
limitation: Short proceedings paper; time-only objective; idealised turbulence.
verification_note: Springer chapter page + arXiv 2103.00329; LNCS volume and pages confirmed.

authors: Chowdhury, R.; Subramani, D. N.
title: Optimal path planning of autonomous marine vehicles in stochastic dynamic ocean flows using a GPU-accelerated algorithm
summary_own_words: Builds and solves a Markov decision process for marine-vehicle routing in uncertain, time-varying ocean flows entirely on a GPU, reporting 600-1000x speed-ups over CPU code. Shows how 'planning under current uncertainty' is done with dynamic programming rather than learning.
supports_project_part: Alternative baseline family (MDP/DP); uncertainty in currents
limitation: Requires an ensemble flow model and a GPU; plans rather than learns a reusable policy.
verification_note: arXiv abstract + IISc eprints + library record; JOE volume/issue/pages/DOI from library record.

authors: Greeley, B.; Brandman, J.; Book, J.; Barron, C.; Landry, B.; Olson, C.
title: On the convergence of a reinforcement learning process to a generalized energy-optimal guidance policy for unmanned underwater vehicles
summary_own_words: Trains a deep-RL guidance agent to minimise energy for an underwater vehicle in current profiles that vary randomly with depth. The learned behaviour is to dive once to explore, then return to the most favourable depth and ride it, trading descent cost against uncertain gain.
supports_project_part: Energy objective in RL guidance; interpretable learned behaviour (good discussion point)
limitation: Currents vary with depth but are time-stationary; abstract-level information only.
verification_note: Library discovery record (Summon) with DOI, abstract and full author names; IEEE Xplore page not opened.

authors: Jiao, Y.; Hang, H.; Merel, J.; Kanso, E.
title: Sensing flow gradients is necessary for learning autonomous underwater navigation
summary_own_words: Studies what an RL swimmer must sense to navigate unsteady flows: knowing local flow speed is enough when the agent knows its global position, but navigating from an egocentric view also needs local flow gradients. A careful look at observation design.
supports_project_part: Observation design (why the 5x5 current patch is a gradient-like signal)
limitation: Idealised wake flows; no energy model or glider constraints.
verification_note: Nature article page + DOAJ/RePEc records + author-hosted PDF; authors, volume, article number confirmed.

authors: Mecanna, S.; Loisy, A.; Eloy, C.
title: A critical assessment of reinforcement learning methods for microswimmer navigation in complex flows
summary_own_words: Benchmarks the RL algorithms commonly used in the flow-navigation literature on one navigation task in three flows (Taylor-Green vortices, ABC flow, 2-D turbulence). Tabular Q-learning and A2C, still widely used, perform poorly and are not robust; deep RL only works with careful choice of algorithm, implementation and tuning. It also points to earlier work where RL failed to beat a simple physics-based heuristic.
supports_project_part: Deep-read gap paper; justifies the strong baselines + multi-seed + CI protocol
limitation: Microswimmer setting (no energy, no vehicle model); journal DOI not opened.
verification_note: arXiv abstract/HTML pages; EPJE publication as stated in the record - confirm DOI on arXiv page.

topic: RL navigation in flows (PPO, double gyre)
authors: Zhang, Y.; ...; Cai, S. (full author list on ScienceDirect page)
title: Efficient navigation in vortical flows based on reinforcement learning and flow field prediction
summary_own_words: Pairs a learned flow-prediction model with a PPO agent so that a vehicle slower than the flow can 'look ahead' when solving a Zermelo-type point-to-point task, tested in a double gyre and a cylinder flow. Code is public (FieldNav-LASS).
supports_project_part: Closest recent method (PPO + double gyre + Zermelo); novelty check
limitation: Time/success focus, not an explicit energy-time trade-off; author list must be copied from the page.
verification_note: ScienceDirect abstract page + official GitHub README (piao233/FieldNav-LASS) giving the DOI. Only first/last author seen.

authors: Gadhvi, R.; Manjanna, S.
title: Khalasi: energy-efficient navigation for surface vehicles in vortical flow fields
summary_own_words: Uses Soft Actor-Critic with only local velocity measurements to make a surface vehicle exploit vortical flows and save energy, reporting 30-50% better energy conservation than prior methods. It argues that grid planners like A*/Dijkstra assume a time-invariant flow.
supports_project_part: Energy-aware RL precedent; argument against static-grid planners
limitation: Not peer reviewed; surface vehicle, not a buoyancy-driven glider.
verification_note: arXiv abstract + HTML pages.

authors: Darvariu, V.-A.; Hawes, N.; et al. (24 authors)
title: Online navigation planning for long-term autonomous operation of underwater gliders
summary_own_words: Models multi-dive glider navigation under uncertain current forecasts as a stochastic shortest-path MDP and solves it online with Monte Carlo Tree Search, re-planning at each surfacing. Tested on real Slocum gliders over about 3 months and 1000 km in the North Sea, improving on straight-to-goal navigation.
supports_project_part: Real-world glider gap: shows what field systems use (planning, straight-to-goal baseline); future-work slide
limitation: Preprint; planner rather than a learned policy; North-Sea-specific results.
verification_note: arXiv abstract + HTML v1/v2.

topic: RL navigation in flows (energy, double gyre)
authors: Braghin, A. M.; Botteghi, N.; Tomasetto, M.; Manzoni, A.; Cazzulani, G.
title: Flow-aware optimal navigation in unsteady flows through reinforcement learning
summary_own_words: Trains TD3 agents to reach arbitrary targets in a parametric chaotic double-gyre flow and compares sensors: velocity-aware agents are more energy-efficient, vorticity-aware ones get closer to targets, and feeding global flow parameters hurts.
supports_project_part: Very close recent work (double gyre, energy, sensing) - must be cited in novelty statement
limitation: Preprint; double gyre only; no classical-planner baseline mentioned in the abstract.
verification_note: arXiv abstract + PDF listing.

authors: Raffin, A.; Hill, A.; Gleave, A.; Kanervisto, A.; Ernestus, M.; Dormann, N.
title: Stable-Baselines3: reliable reinforcement learning implementations
summary_own_words: Describes the Stable-Baselines3 library: tested, documented PyTorch implementations of standard deep-RL algorithms (including PPO), benchmarked against reference code. Cite it as the PPO implementation used.
supports_project_part: Implementation slide; reproducibility
limitation: A software paper: no navigation results; default hyperparameters are not tuned for this task.
verification_note: JMLR abstract page and PDF.

authors: Towers, M.; et al. (16 authors)
title: Gymnasium: a standard interface for reinforcement learning environments
summary_own_words: Presents Gymnasium, the maintained successor of OpenAI Gym, which defines the reset/step API, spaces and wrappers so environments and algorithms interoperate. The project's environment follows this interface and its check_env test.
supports_project_part: Environment design slide
limitation: Pure-Python environments are slow compared with compiled ones (the authors say so).
verification_note: arXiv abstract page.

authors: Agarwal, R.; Schwarzer, M.; Castro, P. S.; Courville, A.; Bellemare, M. G.
title: Deep reinforcement learning at the edge of the statistical precipice
venue: NeurIPS 2021 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34)
summary_own_words: Shows that reporting a single mean over a few training runs is statistically fragile, and recommends bootstrap confidence intervals, performance profiles and the interquartile mean. Outstanding Paper award at NeurIPS 2021.
supports_project_part: Evaluation-protocol slide: 5 training seeds, bootstrap CIs, no single-seed claims
limitation: Designed for multi-task benchmarks; adapting it to one environment family needs care.
verification_note: NeurIPS proceedings PDF + poster page + awards page.

authors: Chassignet, E. P.; Hurlburt, H. E.; Smedstad, O. M.; Halliwell, G. R.; Hogan, P. J.; Wallcraft, A. J.; Baraille, R.; Bleck, R.
title: The HYCOM (HYbrid Coordinate Ocean Model) data assimilative system
summary_own_words: Describes HYCOM, the eddy-resolving ocean model and data-assimilation system behind widely used ocean-current hindcasts and forecasts. It is the obvious source of realistic currents if the synthetic fields are ever replaced.
supports_project_part: Future-work slide (real currents); 'why synthetic fields first' discussion
limitation: System description from 2007; using the data needs large downloads and regridding.
verification_note: NOAA AOML PDF + CU VIVO record + DTIC copy; author list, pages and DOI agree.

authors: Chelton, D. B.; Schlax, M. G.; Samelson, R. M.
title: Global observations of nonlinear mesoscale eddies
summary_own_words: Tracks about 36,000 long-lived ocean eddies in 16 years of satellite sea-surface height and reports how big, strong, long-lived and nonlinear they are and how they drift (mostly westward). Use it to sanity-check the radii and speeds chosen for the synthetic Gaussian eddies.
supports_project_part: ASSUMPTIONS.md: are 5-12 km, 0.1-0.5 m/s eddies realistic?
limitation: Satellite altimetry only resolves mesoscale eddies; compare its radius distribution with the project's small synthetic eddies before claiming realism.
verification_note: DOI resolver page + UMN and WHOI-hosted PDFs; numbers quoted (35,891 eddies, 16 years) appear in the abstract.
